messages:
Amir: Quick sync — thinking about a lean active/active fallback for region-sensitive tenants. Preference: local-region handles reads/writes, but when local is degraded we route to a consented 'escrow' proxy in other regions that only does stateless inference and bounded outputs. Thoughts?

Dina: Sounds reasonable. Biggest risk is accidental cross-border writes. Need an explicit assertion from control plane that the tenant allowed this fallback.

Amir: Agreed. Idea: control plane issues short-lived signed token (residency-assertion) listing approved fallback regions; runtime validates signature before honoring escrow path.

Mike: Operational note: if many tenants failover to the same escrow pool we can easily overload it. Need traffic shaping + per-tenant throttles.

Sara: From product POV, prefer graceful degradation (limited features) rather than full disable. Also customers should be able to opt-out of cross-region fallbacks.

Leah: Legal: even cross-region inference (read-only) can be a problem for some customers. This must be opt-in and surfaced in contracts.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled: escrow-proxy:v0.3 -> dedicated-pool @ 2024-06-12T03:00Z

Dina: RFC follow-up: interface contract should be explicit. Suggest headers: "X-Residency-Mode: resident|escrow" and "X-Residency-Claim: <signed-token>". For guarded tenants reject requests missing a valid claim.

Amir: Example curl for local testing:
```
curl -H "X-Residency-Claim: eyJhbGci..." https://inference.redwood/api/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

Mike: Metrics we need: fallback_count_by_tenant, fallback_p95_latency, and an escrow_pool_cb_state gauge. Also add circuit-breaker defaults (open at 5xx rate or tail latency).

Sara: :thumbsup: I'll add EPIC "escrow-fallback" to the roadmap if infra agrees to the metric/CB work.

Leah: Also request: KMS scoping for the signed tokens and audit log retention for any cross-region calls. Contract addendum to reflect this.

Dina: Edge case: model affinity. If a tenant pins to a large model not available in the escrow region, we must either map to a compatible variant or return a degraded mode. Need a documented fallback mapping table per model.

Amir: Action items:
- Dina: write short RFC for signed tokens + runtime validation (due Mon)
- Mike: run load simulation for escrow pool and propose SLOs (due Wed)
- Sara: draft product note + opt-in flag for customers (due Tue)
- Leah: short legal addendum text for cross-region inference (due Fri)
- Ops: canary scheduled (deploy-bot noted it)
Any objections?

Mike: No objections. I'll instrument fallback metrics and add a dashboard template.

Sara: I'll link the backlog card and start a customer comms draft.

Amir: Attaching a tiny log excerpt from last chaos run for context:
```
[2024-05-10T02:11:45Z] tenant=acme fallback=escrow region=us-east-1 rtt=120ms
[2024-05-10T02:11:46Z] tenant=acme fallback=escrow region=eu-west-1 rtt=190ms
```

Dina: One more infra constraint: do not share model weight caches across tenants on escrow pool. Enforce per-tenant ephemeral mounts or strict cache isolation.

Leah: Agreed. Include explicit "no distribution of model artifacts" clause in the addendum.

Amir: Thanks all — I'll draft the RFC and ping this thread when ready. /cc @Dina @Mike @Sara @Leah
